Subject: Marketplace listing fee evidence & proposed cost allocation for FY26 renewal

Team —

We need to assemble a concise evidence pack for CloudPrime (AWS listing) to support our request for a reduced listing fee / rebate for FY26. AWS has asked for usage breakdowns and marketing co-invest proof before they will consider adjusting the listing rate. The renewal window is in early June, so ask is time-sensitive.

Top-level asks (can owners volunteer?):
- Camila: pull token/usage-by-product (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private) for last 12 months + a short note on how marketplace-driven deals map to our product SKUs. Attach: listing_costs_Q1-4FY26.csv
- Laura: prepare a short narrative (1 page) on GTM activities tied to the listing (co-sell motions, joint webinars, PR) and attach any invoices/POs that show co-marketing spend.
- Vanessa: confirm partner operations evidence (signed onboarding SOWs, co-sell credits applied) and point of contact at CloudPrime (we'll loop them).

Delivery: I'd like an initial packet by EOD 5/22 so I can review before we send to the partner. Put any large files in the secure Drive link and paste here (or attach zipped evidence).

We will propose a cost allocation that splits marketplace listing fee across Hosted vs Dedicated revenue lines (70/30) but open to pushback; need the numbers to justify that split.

Thanks — Sean

Sean —

Thanks for sending this over. Quick triage after spot-checking the archive: overall looks good, but AWS will almost always request the following as separate items (I'd suggest we provide them up front to avoid back-and-forth):
1) Per-account invoicing or order IDs that tie usage rows to customer contracts (CSV is good but add order_id column).
2) A reconciliation showing gross revenue -> net (post discounts/credits) per SKU.
3) Evidence of co-marketing performance (attendance numbers or pipeline influenced) for at least two joint activities in the last 12 months.
4) Signed SOWs that reference marketplace co-sell credits (PDFs).

On allocation: 70/30 is plausible from a consumption standpoint, but AWS' economic reviewer will want to see the logic (usage vs contracted fees). They sometimes prefer an allocation based on billed revenue rather than token consumption. If you can provide both views they can choose; that tends to shorten the review.

Timeline: if you can push the per-account order_ids + gross->net reconciliation today, I can put this into our partner packet and ping the AWS reviewer. Worst-case they ask follow-ups within 3-4 business days.

I'll start the internal escalation once we have those two items.

Cheers — Mike

--
Mike Turner
